# dog

**dog** is a command-line DNS client, like `dig`.

It has colourful output, understands normal command-line argument syntax, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.

![A screenshot of dog making a DNS request](dog-screenshot.png)

## Examples

    dog example.net                          Query a domain using default settings
    dog example.net MX                       ...looking up MX records instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1              ...using a specific nameserver instead
    dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T           ...using TCP rather than UDP
    dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T   As above, but using explicit arguments

## Command-line options

### Query options

    <arguments>              Human-readable host names, nameservers, types, or classes
    -q, --query=HOST         Host name or domain name to query
    -t, --type=TYPE          Type of the DNS record being queried (A, MX, NS...)
    -n, --nameserver=ADDR    Address of the nameserver to send packets to
    --class=CLASS            Network class of the DNS record being queried (IN, CH, HS)

### Sending options

    --edns=SETTING           Whether to OPT in to EDNS (disable, hide, show)
    --txid=NUMBER            Set the transaction ID to a specific value
    -Z=TWEAKS                Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks

### Protocol options

    -U, --udp                Use the DNS protocol over UDP
    -T, --tcp                Use the DNS protocol over TCP
    -S, --tls                Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol
    -H, --https              Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol

### Output options

    -1, --short              Short mode: display nothing but the first result
    -J, --json               Display the output as JSON
    --color, --colour=WHEN   When to colourise the output (always, automatic, never)
    --seconds                Do not format durations, display them as seconds
    --time                   Print how long the response took to arrive

## Installation

Binary downloads of dog are available from the releases section on GitHub for 64-bit Windows, macOS, and Linux targets. They contain the compiled executable, the manual page, and shell completions.

Package manager installations may also be available:
- For Arch Linux: `dog` package
- For Homebrew on macOS: `dog` formula  
- For NixOS: `dogdns` package

## Documentation

For detailed documentation on how to use dog, see the manual page or visit: <https://dns.lookup.dog/>

_dog()
{
    cur=${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}
    prev=${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}

    case "$prev" in
        -'?'|--help|-v|--version)
            return
            ;;

        -t|--type)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'A AAAA CAA CNAME HINFO MX NS PTR SOA SRV TXT' -- "$cur" ) )
            return
            ;;

        --edns)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'disable hide show' -- "$cur" ) )
            return
            ;;

        -Z)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'aa ad bufsize= cd' -- "$cur" ) )
            return
            ;;

        --class)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'IN CH HS' -- "$cur" ) )
            return
            ;;

        --color|--colour)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'always automatic never' -- $cur ) )
            return
            ;;
    esac

    case "$cur" in
        -*)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W '$( _parse_help "$1" )' -- "$cur" ) )
            return
            ;;

        *)
            COMPREPLY=( $( compgen -W 'A AAAA CAA CNAME HINFO MX NS PTR SOA SRV TXT' -- "$cur" ) )
            ;;
    esac
} &&

`-T`, `--tcp`
: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.

`-S`, `--tls`
: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.

`-H`, `--https`
: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.

By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.

Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.

: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.

`-J`, `--json`
: Display the output as JSON.

`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`

`--seconds`
: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.

`--time`
: Print how long the response took to arrive.

============

`--help`
: Displays an overview of the command-line options.

`--version`
: Displays the version of dog being invoked.


ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
=====================

dog responds to the following environment variables:

## `DOG_DEBUG`

Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.


RECORD TYPES
============

dog understands and can interpret the following record types:

`A`
: IPv4 addresses

`AAAA`
: IPv6 addresses

`CAA`
: permitted certificate authorities

`CNAME`
: canonical domain aliases

`HINFO`
: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations

`LOC`
: location information

`MX`
: e-mail server addresses

`NAPTR`
: DDDS rules

`NS`
: domain name servers

`OPT`
: extensions to the DNS protocol

`PTR`
: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups

`SOA`
: administrative information about zones

`SRV`
: IP addresses with port numbers

`SSHFP`
: SSH key fingerprints

`TLSA`
: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes

`TXT`
: arbitrary textual information

When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.

===============

The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:

`aa`
: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.

`ad`
: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.

`bufsize=NUM`
: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.

`cd`
: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.

=============

0
: If everything goes OK.

1
: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.

2
: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.

3
: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.

4
: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.

NAME
====

dog — a command-line DNS client


SYNOPSIS
========

`dog [options] [domains...]`

**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.


EXAMPLES
========

`dog example.net`
: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings

`dog example.net MX`
: ...looking up `MX` records instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
: ...using a specific nameserver instead

`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
: ...using TCP rather than UDP

`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
: As above, but using explicit arguments

=============

`-q`, `--query=HOST`
: Host name or domain name to query.

`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)

`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`

`--class=CLASS`
: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)

import socket, struct, threading, subprocess, sys, time, os, json

def parse_name(data, off):
    labels=[]
    jumped=False
    start=off
    while True:
        if off>=len(data): break
        l=data[off]
        if l==0:
            off+=1
            break
        elif l & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
            if not jumped:
                start=off+2
            ptr=((l&0x3F)<<8)|data[off+1]
            off=ptr
            jumped=True
            continue
        else:
            labels.append(data[off+1:off+1+l])
            off+=1+l
    return labels, (start if jumped else off)

def encode_name(name):
    # name list of bytes labels or dotted string/bytes
    if isinstance(name, (bytes,str)):
        if isinstance(name,str): name=name.encode()
        if name==b"" or name==b".": return b"\x00"
        parts=name.rstrip(b'.').split(b'.')
    else:
        parts=name
    out=b""
    for p in parts:
        out+=bytes([len(p)])+p
    out+=b"\x00"
    return out

def build_response(req, answers=None, authorities=None, additionals=None, rcode=0, flags_extra=0, truncate=False, edns_answer=None):
    # answers list of (name_labels_or_str, type, class, ttl, rdata_bytes)
    answers=answers or []
    authorities=authorities or []
    additionals=additionals or []
    txid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar = struct.unpack("!HHHHHH", req[:12])
    # parse question
    labels, off = parse_name(req,12)
    qtype,qclass = struct.unpack("!HH", req[off:off+4])
    question = req[12:off+4]
    # response flags: QR=1, copy opcode/RD? set RA=1? We'll return flags: QR, RD copied, RA, rcode
    rd = flags & 0x0100
    newflags = 0x8000 | rd | 0x0080 | rcode | flags_extra
    if truncate: newflags |= 0x0200
    header = struct.pack("!HHHHHH", txid, newflags, 1, len(answers), len(authorities), len(additionals)+(1 if edns_answer else 0))
    body=question
    def enc_rr(rr):
        name, typ, cls, ttl, rdata = rr
        # if name is "ptr" use compression pointer to question (12)
        if name=="PTR_QUESTION":
            out=b"\xc0\x0c"
        elif isinstance(name, bytes) and name.startswith(b"\xc0"):
            out=name
        else:
            out=encode_name(name)
        out+=struct.pack("!HHIH", typ, cls, ttl, len(rdata))+rdata
        return out
    for rr in answers: body+=enc_rr(rr)
    for rr in authorities: body+=enc_rr(rr)
    for rr in additionals: body+=enc_rr(rr)
    if edns_answer:
        body+=edns_answer
    return header+body

class Server:
    def __init__(self, port=53535, responder=None, tcp=False):
        self.port=port
        self.responder=responder or (lambda req: build_response(req, []))
        self.requests=[]
        self.tcp=tcp
        self.sock=None
        self.thread=None
        self.stop=False
    def start(self):
        if self.tcp:
            self.sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
            self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1)
            self.sock.bind(("127.0.0.1",self.port))
            self.sock.listen(5)
            self.sock.settimeout(0.5)
        else:
            self.sock=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
            self.sock.bind(("127.0.0.1",self.port))
            self.sock.settimeout(0.5)
        self.thread=threading.Thread(target=self.loop, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
    def loop(self):
        while not self.stop:
            try:
                if self.tcp:
                    conn,addr=self.sock.accept()
                    conn.settimeout(2)
                    try:
                        while True:
                            hdr=conn.recv(2)
                            if not hdr: break
                            length=struct.unpack("!H",hdr)[0]
                            data=b""
                            while len(data)<length:
                                chunk=conn.recv(length-len(data))
                                if not chunk: break
                                data+=chunk
                            self.requests.append(data)
                            resp=self.responder(data)
                            if resp is not None:
                                conn.sendall(struct.pack("!H",len(resp))+resp)
                    except Exception as e:
                        #print("tcp err",e)
                        pass
                    finally:
                        conn.close()
                else:
                    data,addr=self.sock.recvfrom(65535)
                    self.requests.append(data)
                    resp=self.responder(data)
                    if resp is not None:
                        self.sock.sendto(resp,addr)
            except socket.timeout:
                continue
            except Exception as e:
                #print("server err",e)
                continue
    def close(self):
        self.stop=True
        try: self.sock.close()
        except: pass

def run_dog(args, env=None, timeout=5):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=timeout)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode(errors='surrogateescape'), p.stderr.decode(errors='surrogateescape')

def describe_req(data):
    if len(data)<12: return f"short {data.hex()}"
    txid,flags,qd,an,ns,ar = struct.unpack("!HHHHHH", data[:12])
    parts=[f"txid={txid} ({txid:#x}) flags={flags:04x} qd={qd} an={an} ns={ns} ar={ar} len={len(data)}"]
    off=12
    for i in range(qd):
        labels,off2=parse_name(data,off)
        qtype,qclass=struct.unpack("!HH", data[off2:off2+4])
        parts.append(f" Q{i}: labels={[l for l in labels]} type={qtype} class={qclass}")
        off=off2+4
    # remaining sections parse RR
    total=an+ns+ar
    for i in range(total):
        if off>=len(data): break
        labels,off2=parse_name(data,off)
        if off2+10>len(data): parts.append(f" RR truncated"); break
        typ,cls,ttl,rdlen=struct.unpack("!HHIH", data[off2:off2+10])
        rdata=data[off2+10:off2+10+rdlen]
        parts.append(f" RR{i}: labels={labels} type={typ} class/udp={cls} ttl/ext={ttl} ({ttl:#x}) rdlen={rdlen} rdata={rdata.hex()}")
        off=off2+10+rdlen
    if off < len(data):
        parts.append(f" trailing={data[off:].hex()}")
    return "".join(parts)

import sys, os, ssl, threading, socket, struct, subprocess, time
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import *

os.makedirs("/tmp/certs", exist_ok=True)
if not os.path.exists("/tmp/certs/cert.pem"):
    subprocess.run(["openssl","req","-x509","-newkey","rsa:2048","-nodes","-keyout","/tmp/certs/key.pem","-out","/tmp/certs/cert.pem","-days","3650","-subj","/CN=localhost","-addext","subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"], check=True, capture_output=True)

# TLS server (DoT): accept TLS, then read 2-byte length DNS, respond
def tls_server(port=53541):
    ctx=ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain("/tmp/certs/cert.pem","/tmp/certs/key.pem")
    # ctx ALPN?
    try:
        ctx.set_alpn_protocols(["dot","h2","http/1.1"])
    except: pass
    raw=socket.socket()
    raw.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1)
    raw.bind(("127.0.0.1",port)); raw.listen(5); raw.settimeout(10)
    conn,addr=raw.accept()
    print("TCP accepted",addr)
    try:
        ssock=ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
        print("TLS ok", ssock.version(), ssock.selected_alpn_protocol(), ssock.cipher())
        hdr=ssock.recv(2)
        print("hdr",hdr)
        if hdr:
            length=struct.unpack("!H",hdr)[0]
            data=ssock.recv(length)
            print("data",describe_req(data))
            resp=build_response(data, [("PTR_QUESTION",1,1,3600,socket.inet_aton("7.7.7.7"))])
            ssock.sendall(struct.pack("!H",len(resp))+resp)
            time.sleep(0.5)
        ssock.close()
    except Exception as e:
        print("TLS server error",type(e),e)
    finally:
        raw.close()

]:

    rc,out,err=run_dog(args)
    print(args, rc, repr(out), repr(err))
    break
t.join(timeout=3)

import sys, os, ssl, threading, socket, struct, subprocess, time
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import *

def one(args, port=53541):
    res={}
    ctx=ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain("/tmp/certs/cert.pem","/tmp/certs/key.pem")
    ctx.sni_callback=lambda ssock,name,ctxi: res.update(sni=name)
    raw=socket.socket(); raw.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); raw.bind(("127.0.0.1",port)); raw.listen(5); raw.settimeout(5)
    def serve():
        try:
            conn,addr=raw.accept(); res['peer']=addr
            ssock=ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
            res['alpn']=ssock.selected_alpn_protocol()
            hdr=ssock.recv(2)
            if hdr:
                ln=struct.unpack("!H",hdr)[0]; data=b""
                while len(data)<ln: data+=ssock.recv(ln-len(data))
                res['req']=describe_req(data)
                resp=build_response(data,[("PTR_QUESTION",1,1,60,socket.inet_aton("7.7.7.7"))])
                ssock.sendall(struct.pack("!H",len(resp))+resp); time.sleep(0.2)
            ssock.close()
        except Exception as e:
            res['error']=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        finally: raw.close()
    t=threading.Thread(target=serve,daemon=True); t.start(); time.sleep(0.2)
    env={"SSL_CERT_FILE":"/tmp/certs/cert.pem","DOG_DEBUG":"1"}

        while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data:

        header,sep,body=data.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")

                cl=int(line.split(b":",1)[1].strip())

            body+=ssock.recv(4096)
        results['body']=body

        firstline=header.split(b"\r\n")[0].decode()
        results['request_line']=firstline
        dns_bytes=None
        if body and cl:
            dns_bytes=body

            # get query param
            from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
            parts=firstline.split()
            url=parts[1] if len(parts)>1 else ""
            qs=parse_qs(urlparse(url).query)
            if 'dns' in qs:
                b64=qs['dns'][0]
                b64+= "="*(-len(b64)%4)
                dns_bytes=base64.urlsafe_b64decode(b64)
        results['dns_req']=describe_req(dns_bytes) if dns_bytes else None
        if dns_bytes:
            resp_dns=build_response(dns_bytes,[("PTR_QUESTION",1,1,3600,socket.inet_aton("8.8.8.8"))])
        else:
            resp_dns=b""
        if mode=="normal":

        elif mode=="404":
            http=b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
        elif mode=="wrong_ct":
            http=(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: "+str(len(resp_dns)).encode()+b"\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"+resp_dns)
        elif mode=="json_ct":
            http=(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/dns-json\r\nContent-Length: "+str(len(resp_dns)).encode()+b"\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"+resp_dns)
        else:
            http=b"HTTP/1.1 500 Internal\r\nContent-Length: 5\r\n\r\nhello"
        ssock.sendall(http)
        time.sleep(0.3); ssock.close()
    except Exception as e:
        results['error']=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        import traceback; traceback.print_exc()
    finally:
        raw.close()

def one(url, mode="normal", extra=[]):
    results={}
    t=threading.Thread(target=https_server,args=(53548,mode,results),daemon=True); t.start(); time.sleep(0.3)
    env={"SSL_CERT_FILE":"/tmp/certs/cert.pem","DOG_DEBUG":"trace"}
    rc,out,err=run_dog(extra+["-H","-n",url,"example.com"], env=env)
    t.join(timeout=3)
    print("URL",url,"mode",mode,"RC",rc,"OUT",repr(out))
    # strip ansi for err relevant
    import re
    clean=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',err)
    for line in clean.splitlines():
        if 'https' in line.lower() or 'Error' in line or 'Got' in line:
            print(" ERRline:",line[:1000])
    print(" RESULTS",{k:(v.decode(errors='replace') if isinstance(v,bytes) else v) for k,v in results.items()})
    time.sleep(0.6)

from https_probe import *

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import *

def cs(b): return bytes([len(b)])+b

 "LOC":(29, bytes([0,0x12,0x16,0x13])+struct.pack("!III",1<<31,1<<31,10000000)),
}
def run_case(name,code,rdata,rdlen):
    def responder(req):
        txid=req[:2]; header=txid+b"\x81\x80"+struct.pack("!HHHH",1,1,0,0); q=encode_name("example.com")+struct.pack("!HH",1,1); ans=b"\xc0\x0c"+struct.pack("!HHIH",code,1,3600,rdlen)+rdata; return header+q+ans
    srv=Server(53560,responder); srv.start()
    try:
        rc,out,err=run_dog(["example.com","@127.0.0.1:53560"])
        print(name,"phys",len(rdata),"rdlen",rdlen,"rc",rc,"out",repr(out),"err",repr(err))
    finally: srv.close(); time.sleep(0.55)

for name,(code,rd) in valid.items():
    for rdlen in list(range(0, len(rd)+2)):
        run_case(name,code,rd,rdlen)

# capture TTY full via pty to file for analysis later
import pty, os
def capture(args):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.execv("./executable",["./executable"]+args)
    chunks=b""
    while True:
        try:
            d=os.read(fd,4096)
            if not d: break
            chunks+=d
        except OSError: break
    os.waitpid(pid,0)
    return chunks

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from probe import *
import threading, time, re
# Custom TCP server sends response in chunks with delay
class FragTCP:
    def __init__(self, chunksizes, delay=0.2):
        self.chunksizes=chunksizes; self.delay=delay
    def start(self,port=53575):
        self.sock=socket.socket(); self.sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET,socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); self.sock.bind(('127.0.0.1',port)); self.sock.listen(1)
        self.thread=threading.Thread(target=self.run,daemon=True); self.thread.start()
    def run(self):
        conn,addr=self.sock.accept()
        hdr=conn.recv(2); ln=struct.unpack("!H",hdr)[0]; data=b""
        while len(data)<ln: data+=conn.recv(ln-len(data))
        resp=build_response(data,[("PTR_QUESTION",1,1,60,socket.inet_aton("4.4.4.4"))])
        payload=struct.pack("!H",len(resp))+resp
        pos=0
        for sz in self.chunksizes:
            if pos>=len(payload): break
            chunk=payload[pos:pos+sz]; conn.sendall(chunk); pos+=len(chunk); time.sleep(self.delay)
        if pos<len(payload): conn.sendall(payload[pos:])
        time.sleep(0.3); conn.close(); self.sock.close()

for chunks in [[1,1,5],[2,2,10],[47],[10,10,10],[1],[0]]:
    srv=FragTCP(chunks); srv.start(); time.sleep(0.2)
    rc,out,err=run_dog(["-T","example.com","@127.0.0.1:53575"],env={"DOG_DEBUG":"1"})
    clean=re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m','',err)
    rel=[l.strip() for l in clean.splitlines() if 'tcp' in l.lower() or 'Error' in l]
    print("chunks",chunks,rc,repr(out)); [print(" ",l) for l in rel]
    time.sleep(0.6)

def nameprep(label):
    # Map
    newlabel = []
    for c in label:
        if stringprep.in_table_b1(c):
            # Map to nothing
            continue
        newlabel.append(stringprep.map_table_b2(c))
    label = "".join(newlabel)

    # Normalize
    label = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", label)

    # Prohibit
    for c in label:
        if stringprep.in_table_c12(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c22(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c3(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c4(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c5(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c6(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c7(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c8(c) or \
           stringprep.in_table_c9(c):
            raise UnicodeError("Invalid character %r" % c)

    # Check bidi
    RandAL = [stringprep.in_table_d1(x) for x in label]
    if any(RandAL):
        # There is a RandAL char in the string. Must perform further
        # tests:
        # 1) The characters in section 5.8 MUST be prohibited.
        # This is table C.8, which was already checked
        # 2) If a string contains any RandALCat character, the string
        # MUST NOT contain any LCat character.
        if any(stringprep.in_table_d2(x) for x in label):
            raise UnicodeError("Violation of BIDI requirement 2")
        # 3) If a string contains any RandALCat character, a
        # RandALCat character MUST be the first character of the
        # string, and a RandALCat character MUST be the last
        # character of the string.
        if not RandAL[0] or not RandAL[-1]:
            raise UnicodeError("Violation of BIDI requirement 3")

    return label

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DNS wire parsing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Failure(Exception):
    def __init__(self, phase, message):
        Exception.__init__(self, message)
        self.phase = phase
        self.message = message

class MalformedPacket(Exception):
    def __init__(self, detail):
        Exception.__init__(self, detail)
        self.detail = detail

    @property
    def message(self):
        return "Malformed packet: " + self.detail

class Query(object):
    __slots__ = ("name", "type_code", "class_code")
    def __init__(self, name, type_code, class_code):
        self.name = name
        self.type_code = type_code
        self.class_code = class_code

class Record(object):
    __slots__ = ("name", "type_code", "class_code", "ttl", "data", "is_opt",
                 "opt_udp", "opt_higher", "opt_version", "opt_flags", "opt_data")
    def __init__(self, name, type_code, class_code, ttl, data):
        self.name = name
        self.type_code = type_code
        self.class_code = class_code
        self.ttl = ttl
        self.data = data
        self.is_opt = False
        self.opt_udp = None
        self.opt_higher = None
        self.opt_version = None
        self.opt_flags = None
        self.opt_data = None

class DnsResponse(object):
    __slots__ = ("txid", "flags", "error_code", "truncated", "queries", "answers", "authorities", "additionals")
    def __init__(self):
        self.txid = 0
        self.flags = 0
        self.error_code = 0
        self.truncated = False
        self.queries = []
        self.answers = []
        self.authorities = []
        self.additionals = []

def _format_binary(value):
    digits = format(value, "b")
    if len(digits) < 6:
        digits = "0" * (6 - len(digits)) + digits
    return "0b" + digits

_RCODE_DEBUG_NAMES = {
    1: "FormatError", 2: "ServerFailure", 3: "NXDomain",
    4: "NotImplemented", 5: "QueryRefused",
}
_RCODE_TEXT = {
    1: "Format Error", 2: "Server Failure", 3: "NXDomain",
    4: "Not Implemented", 5: "Query Refused",
}

def _flags_debug_node(flags):

    else:
        error_node = _TupleVariant("Some", [_TupleVariant("Other", [error_code])])
    return _Struct("Flags", [
        ("response", response),
        ("opcode", opcode_node),
        ("authoritative", bool(flags & 0x0400)),
        ("truncated", bool(flags & 0x0200)),
        ("recursion_desired", bool(flags & 0x0100)),
        ("recursion_available", bool(flags & 0x0080)),
        ("authentic_data", bool(flags & 0x0020)),

class Wire(object):
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = bytes(data)
        self.pos = 0

    def _insufficient(self):
        log_error("dns::wire", 'IO error -> Error { kind: UnexpectedEof, message: "failed to fill whole buffer" }')
        raise MalformedPacket("insufficient data")

    def read(self, count):
        if count < 0 or self.pos + count > len(self.data):
            self._insufficient()
        chunk = self.data[self.pos:self.pos + count]
        self.pos += count
        return chunk

    def read_at(self, offset, count):
        if count < 0 or offset < 0 or offset + count > len(self.data):
            self._insufficient()
        return self.data[offset:offset + count]

    def read_u8(self):
        return self.read(1)[0]

    def read_u16(self):
        return struct.unpack("!H", self.read(2))[0]

    def read_u32(self):
        return struct.unpack("!I", self.read(4))[0]

    def read_labels(self):
        labels, new_pos = self._read_labels_at(self.pos, [])
        self.pos = new_pos
        return labels_from_wire_segments(labels)

    def _read_labels_at(self, offset, previous_offsets):
        labels = []
        pos = offset
        while True:
            length = self.read_at(pos, 1)[0]
            pos += 1
            if length == 0:
                break
            if length & 0xC0 == 0xC0:
                second = self.read_at(pos, 1)[0]
                pos += 1
                pointer = ((length & 0x3F) << 8) | second
                if pointer in previous_offsets:
                    log_warn("dns::strings", "Hit previous offset (%d) decoding string" % pointer)
                    raise MalformedPacket(
                        "too much recursion: [%s]" % ", ".join(str(item) for item in previous_offsets))
                log_trace("dns::strings", "Backtracking to offset %d" % pointer)
                sub_labels, _ignored = self._read_labels_at(pointer, previous_offsets + [pointer])
                log_trace("dns::strings", "Coming back to %d" % pos)
                labels.extend(sub_labels)
                break
            segment = self.read_at(pos, length)
            labels.append(lossy_utf8(segment))
            pos += length
        return labels, pos

    def read_character_string(self):
        length = self.read_u8()
        return self.read(length)

    # Record-data parsing -------------------------------------------------

    def _verify_record_length(self, start, expected_length):
        read_amount = self.pos - start
        if read_amount != expected_length:
            raise MalformedPacket(
                "length %d was specified, but read %d bytes" % (expected_length, read_amount))

    def _parse_record_data(self, type_code, rd_length):
        start = self.pos
        if type_code == 1:  # A
            if rd_length != 4:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 4, got %d" % rd_length)
            address = ".".join(str(byte) for byte in self.read(4))
            log_trace("dns::record::a", "Parsed IPv4 address -> %s" % address)
            return {"kind": "A", "address": address}
        if type_code == 28:  # AAAA
            if rd_length != 16:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 16, got %d" % rd_length)
            address = ipaddress.IPv6Address(self.read(16)).compressed
            log_trace("dns::record::aaaa", "Parsed IPv6 address -> %s" % address)
            return {"kind": "AAAA", "address": address}
        if type_code in (2, 5, 12):  # NS, CNAME, PTR
            labels = self.read_labels()
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            kind = {2: "NS", 5: "CNAME", 12: "PTR"}[type_code]
            return {"kind": kind, "labels": labels}
        if type_code == 13:  # HINFO
            cpu = self.read_character_string()
            os_name = self.read_character_string()
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "HINFO", "cpu": cpu, "os": os_name}
        if type_code == 15:  # MX
            preference = self.read_u16()
            labels = self.read_labels()
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "MX", "preference": preference, "labels": labels}
        if type_code == 16:  # TXT
            messages = []
            while True:
                messages.append(self.read_character_string())
                if self.pos - start >= rd_length:
                    break
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "TXT", "messages": messages}
        if type_code == 6:  # SOA
            mname = self.read_labels()
            rname = self.read_labels()
            serial = self.read_u32()
            refresh = self.read_u32()
            retry = self.read_u32()
            expire = self.read_u32()
            minimum = self.read_u32()
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "SOA", "mname": mname, "rname": rname, "serial": serial,
                    "refresh": refresh, "retry": retry, "expire": expire, "minimum": minimum}
        if type_code == 33:  # SRV
            priority = self.read_u16()
            weight = self.read_u16()
            port = self.read_u16()

            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "SRV", "priority": priority, "weight": weight, "port": port, "labels": labels}

            flag_byte = self.read_u8()
            tag = self.read_character_string()
            consumed = 2 + len(tag)
            remaining = rd_length - consumed
            if remaining < 0:
                remaining = 0
            value = self.read(remaining)
            # The reference does not apply the generic length check here.
            return {"kind": "CAA", "critical": bool(flag_byte & 0x80), "tag": tag, "value": value}
        if type_code == 29:  # LOC
            version = self.read_u8()
            if version != 0:
                raise MalformedPacket("record specifies version %d, expected up to 0" % version)
            if rd_length != 16:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 16, got %d" % rd_length)
            size = self.read_u8()
            horiz = self.read_u8()
            vert = self.read_u8()
            latitude = self.read_u32()
            longitude = self.read_u32()
            altitude = self.read_u32()
            return {"kind": "LOC", "size": size, "horiz": horiz, "vert": vert,
                    "latitude": latitude, "longitude": longitude, "altitude": altitude}
        if type_code == 35:  # NAPTR
            order = self.read_u16()
            preference = self.read_u16()
            flags = self.read_character_string()
            service = self.read_character_string()
            regex = self.read_character_string()
            labels = self.read_labels()
            self._verify_record_length(start, rd_length)
            return {"kind": "NAPTR", "order": order, "preference": preference,
                    "flags": flags, "service": service, "regex": regex, "labels": labels}
        if type_code == 44:  # SSHFP
            algorithm = self.read_u8()
            fp_type = self.read_u8()
            if rd_length < 3:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be at least 3, got %d" % rd_length)
            fingerprint = self.read(rd_length - 2)
            return {"kind": "SSHFP", "algorithm": algorithm, "fingerprint_type": fp_type,
                    "fingerprint": fingerprint.hex()}
        if type_code == 52:  # TLSA
            usage = self.read_u8()
            selector = self.read_u8()
            matching = self.read_u8()
            if rd_length < 4:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be at least 4, got %d" % rd_length)
            cert = self.read(rd_length - 3)
            return {"kind": "TLSA", "certificate_usage": usage, "selector": selector,
                    "matching_type": matching, "certificate_data": cert.hex()}
        if type_code == 61:  # OPENPGPKEY
            if rd_length < 1:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be at least 1, got %d" % rd_length)
            key = self.read(rd_length)
            return {"kind": "OPENPGPKEY", "key": base64.b64encode(key).decode("ascii")}
        if type_code == 108:  # EUI48
            if rd_length != 6:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 6, got %d" % rd_length)
            ident = "-".join("%02x" % byte for byte in self.read(6))
            return {"kind": "EUI48", "identifier": ident}
        if type_code == 109:  # EUI64
            if rd_length != 8:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 8, got %d" % rd_length)
            ident = "-".join("%02x" % byte for byte in self.read(8))
            return {"kind": "EUI64", "identifier": ident}
        if type_code == 256:  # URI
            priority = self.read_u16()
            weight = self.read_u16()
            if rd_length < 5:
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be at least 5, got %d" % rd_length)
            target = self.read(rd_length - 4)
            return {"kind": "URI", "priority": priority, "weight": weight, "target": target}
        # Everything else is an opaque byte string.
        return {"kind": "OTHER", "bytes": list(self.read(rd_length))}

    def read_query(self):
        name = self.read_labels()
        qtype = self.read_u16()
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read qtype number -> %d" % qtype)
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Found qtype -> %s" % type_debug_compact(qtype))
        qclass = self.read_u16()
        # The reference logs the qtype again in the qclass trace message.
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read qclass -> %s" % type_debug_compact(qtype))
        return Query(name, qtype, qclass)

    def read_record(self):
        name = self.read_labels()
        type_code = self.read_u16()
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read qtype number -> %d" % type_code)
        if type_code == 41:  # OPT pseudo-record
            udp_payload = self.read_u16()
            log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed UDP payload size -> %d" % udp_payload)
            higher = self.read_u8()
            log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed higher bits -> %s" % _format_binary(higher))
            version = self.read_u8()
            log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed EDNS(0) version -> %d" % version)
            flags = self.read_u16()
            log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed flags -> %s" % _format_binary(flags))
            rd_length = self.read_u16()
            log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed data length -> %d" % rd_length)
            data_bytes = self.read(rd_length)
            if log_enabled("TRACE"):
                data_node = _List([byte for byte in data_bytes])
                log_trace("dns::record::opt", "Parsed data -> %s" % rust_debug_pretty(data_node))
            record = Record(name, 41, None, None, {"kind": "OPT"})
            record.is_opt = True
            record.opt_udp = udp_payload
            record.opt_higher = higher
            record.opt_version = version
            record.opt_flags = flags
            record.opt_data = list(data_bytes)
            return record

        log_trace("dns::wire", "Found qtype -> %s" % type_debug_compact(type_code))
        class_code = self.read_u16()
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read qclass -> %s" % type_debug_compact(type_code))
        ttl = self.read_u32()
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read TTL -> %d" % ttl)
        rd_length = self.read_u16()
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read record length -> %d" % rd_length)
        if type_code in _TYPE_PARSED:
            log_info("dns::wire", "Parsing %s record (type %d, len %d)" % (_TYPE_PARSED[type_code], type_code, rd_length))
        data = self._parse_record_data(type_code, rd_length)
        return Record(name, type_code, class_code, ttl, data)

def parse_response(data):
    log_info("dns::wire", "Parsing response")
    log_trace("dns::wire", "Bytes -> [%s]" % ", ".join(str(byte) for byte in data))
    wire = Wire(data)
    response = DnsResponse()
    response.txid = wire.read_u16()
    log_trace("dns::wire", "Read txid -> %d" % response.txid)
    response.flags = wire.read_u16()
    response.error_code = response.flags & 0xF
    response.truncated = bool(response.flags & 0x0200)
    if log_enabled("TRACE"):
        log_trace("dns::wire", "Read flags -> %s" % rust_debug_pretty(_flags_debug_node(response.flags)))
    query_count = wire.read_u16()
    answer_count = wire.read_u16()
    authority_count = wire.read_u16()
    additional_count = wire.read_u16()

    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx query from response" % query_count)
    for _ in range(query_count):
        response.queries.append(wire.read_query())
    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx answer from response" % answer_count)
    for _ in range(answer_count):
        response.answers.append(wire.read_record())
    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx authority from response" % authority_count)
    for _ in range(authority_count):
        response.authorities.append(wire.read_record())
    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx additional answer from response" % additional_count)
    for _ in range(additional_count):
        response.additionals.append(wire.read_record())
    return response

# Building requests ---------------------------------------------------------

def build_request_packet(options, domain, type_code, class_code, txid):
    flags = 0x0100  # recursion desired
    if options.tweak_aa:
        flags |= 0x0400
    if options.tweak_ad:
        flags |= 0x0020
    if options.tweak_cd:
        flags |= 0x0010
    additional_count = 0 if options.edns == "disable" else 1
    packet = bytearray()
    packet.extend(struct.pack("!HHHHHH", txid & 0xFFFF, flags, 1, 0, 0, additional_count))
    packet.extend(domain.wire_bytes())
    packet.extend(struct.pack("!HH", type_code & 0xFFFF, class_code & 0xFFFF))
    if additional_count:
        udp_size = options.tweak_bufsize if options.tweak_bufsize is not None else 512
        packet.append(0)
        packet.extend(struct.pack("!HHIH", 41, udp_size & 0xFFFF, 0, 0))
    return bytes(packet)

    log_trace("dns::wire", "Bytes -> [%s]" % ", ".join(str(byte) for byte in data))
    wire = Wire(data)

    response.txid = wire.read_u16()

    authority_count = wire.read_u16()
    additional_count = wire.read_u16()

    for _ in range(query_count):

    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx answer from response" % answer_count)
    for _ in range(answer_count):
        response.answers.append(wire.read_record())
    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx authority from response" % authority_count)
    for _ in range(authority_count):
        response.authorities.append(wire.read_record())
    log_debug("dns::wire", "Reading %dx additional answer from response" % additional_count)
    for _ in range(additional_count):
        response.additionals.append(wire.read_record())

# Building requests ---------------------------------------------------------

def build_request_packet(options, domain, type_code, class_code, txid):
    flags = 0x0100  # recursion desired
    if options.tweak_aa:
        flags |= 0x0400
    if options.tweak_ad:
        flags |= 0x0020
    if options.tweak_cd:
        flags |= 0x0010
    additional_count = 0 if options.edns == "disable" else 1
    packet = bytearray()
    packet.extend(struct.pack("!HHHHHH", txid & 0xFFFF, flags, 1, 0, 0, additional_count))
    packet.extend(domain.wire_bytes())
    packet.extend(struct.pack("!HH", type_code & 0xFFFF, class_code & 0xFFFF))
    if additional_count:
        udp_size = options.tweak_bufsize if options.tweak_bufsize is not None else 512
        packet.append(0)
        packet.extend(struct.pack("!HHIH", 41, udp_size & 0xFFFF, 0, 0))
    return bytes(packet)

    def _verify_record_length(self, start, expected_length, target=None, description=None, close_paren=True):
        read_amount = self.pos - start
        if read_amount == expected_length:
            if target is not None and description is not None:
                log_trace(target, "Length is correct")
            return
        if target is not None and description is not None:
            log_warn(
                target,
                "Length is incorrect (stated length %d, %s length %d%s" % (
                    expected_length, description, read_amount, ")" if close_paren else ""))
        raise MalformedPacket(
            "length %d was specified, but read %d bytes" % (expected_length, read_amount))

    def _read_character_string_logged(self, target, length_message, value_message):
        length = self.read_u8()
        log_trace(target, "%s -> %d" % (length_message, length))
        value = self.read(length)
        log_trace(target, "%s -> %s" % (value_message, rust_debug_str(lossy_utf8(value))))
        return value

    @staticmethod
    def _hex_list_pretty(values):
        return rust_debug_pretty(_List([_Bare("0x%x" % byte) for byte in values]))

    @staticmethod
    def _loc_position_debug(raw, is_latitude):
        offset = raw - (1 << 31)
        limit = (90 if is_latitude else 180) * 3600 * 1000
        if abs(offset) > limit:
            return "None"
        if is_latitude:
            direction = "North" if offset >= 0 else "South"
        else:
            direction = "East" if offset >= 0 else "West"
        total = abs(offset)
        degrees, remainder = divmod(total, 3600000)
        minutes, remainder = divmod(remainder, 60000)
        seconds, millis = divmod(remainder, 1000)
        return ("Some(Position { degrees: %d, arcminutes: %d, arcseconds: %d, "
                "milliarcseconds: %d, direction: %s })" % (degrees, minutes, seconds, millis, direction))

    def _parse_record_data(self, type_code, rd_length):

                log_warn("dns::record::a", "Length is incorrect (record length %d, but should be four)" % rd_length)
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 4, got %d" % rd_length)

            log_trace("dns::record::a", "Parsed IPv4 address -> %s" % address)
            return {"kind": "A", "address": address}

            if rd_length != 16:
                log_warn("dns::record::aaaa", "Length is incorrect (stated length %d, but should be sixteen)" % rd_length)
                raise MalformedPacket("record length should be 16, got %d" % rd_length)
            address = ipaddress.IPv6Address(self.read(16)).compressed
            log_trace("dns::record::aaaa", "Parsed IPv6 address -> %s" % address)
            return {"kind": "AAAA", "address": address}

            log_trace("dns::record::ptr", "Parsed cname -> %s" % labels.compact_debug())

            log_trace("dns::record::soa", "Parsed expire limit -> %d" % expire)
